firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
I believe that relying solely on "bottom-up" approaches like reinforcement learning has inherent limitations when it comes to training AI for long-term action planning. However, if we have access to "expert" action planning data—similar to gameplay logs of players clearing a game—we should be able to train models on action planning using a "top-down" approach. Recently, the human gameplay data from the ARC-AGI-3 environment was released here: [ARC-AGI-3 Human Dataset](https://arcprize.org/blog/arc-agi-3-human-dataset) To make this data more accessible for implementation, I’ve registered the dataset on Hugging Face. If we can leverage imitation learning to mimic how humans solve these tasks, I'm confident it will give AI a massive boost in long-term action planning.
The repository is here: 👉[magic-sword/arc_agi_3_public_demo_human_testing](https://huggingface.co/datasets/magic-sword/arc_agi_3_public_demo_human_testing) I have also published a Kaggle Notebook that demonstrates both **how I uploaded this data to Hugging Face** and **how to load and use it** in your own workflows. You can check it out here: 👉 [ARC-AGI-3 Public Demo Human Testing (Hugging Face)](https://www.kaggle.com/code/magicsword001/arc-agi-3-public-demo-human-testing-hugging-face?scriptVersionId=325811099) Here is a quick overview of how you can use it: ### 1. Analyzing with Pandas DataFrame ```python import pandas as pd from datasets import load_dataset repo_id = "magic-sword/arc_agi_3_public_demo_human_testing" dataset = load_dataset(repo_id, split="train") # Exclude the heavy 'trajectory' column to save memory light_dataset = dataset.remove_columns(['trajectory']) df = light_dataset.to_pandas() ``` ⚠️ Note on Memory: The trajectory data is quite large. If you try to convert the entire dataset (including trajectories) directly into a Pandas DataFrame, your Kaggle notebook will likely crash due to an OOM (Out of Memory) error. When using DataFrames, please drop the trajectory column first and parse the trajectory data separately/individually. ### 2. Extracting and Using Trajectory Data (Streaming) ```python import json from datasets import load_dataset repo_id = "magic-sword/arc_agi_3_public_demo_human_testing" stream_dataset = load_dataset(repo_id, split="train", streaming=True) # Process trajectories individually for idx, record in enumerate(stream_dataset.take(5)): trajectory_obj = json.loads(record['trajectory']) ``` ## Future Plans Looking ahead, I want to enhance this dataset by adding explanations of the "human thought process" behind each step in the trajectory. Mimicking not just the actions, but the actual reasoning behind them, could be a powerful weapon for AI long-term planning. That said, annotating all this reasoning by myself is going to be a massive, time-consuming task... What do you think? I'd love to hear your thoughts on utilizing this human dataset for ARC-AGI-3, or any feedback on the notebook!
firstMessage.content:
I believe that relying solely on "bottom-up" approaches like reinforcement learning has inherent limitations when it comes to training AI for long-term action planning. However, if we have access to "expert" action planning data—similar to gameplay logs of players clearing a game—we should be able to train models on action planning using a "top-down" approach.

Recently, the human gameplay data from the ARC-AGI-3 environment was released here: ARC-AGI-3 Human Dataset

To make this data more accessible for implementation, I’ve registered the dataset on Hugging Face. If we can leverage imitation learning to mimic how humans solve these tasks, I'm confident it will give AI a massive boost in long-term action planning.
The repository is here: 👉magic-sword/arc_agi_3_public_demo_human_testing

I have also published a Kaggle Notebook that demonstrates both how I uploaded this data to Hugging Face and how to load and use it in your own workflows. You can check it out here: 👉 ARC-AGI-3 Public Demo Human Testing (Hugging Face)

Here is a quick overview of how you can use it:

1. Analyzing with Pandas DataFrame

import pandas as pd
from datasets import load_dataset

repo_id = "magic-sword/arc_agi_3_public_demo_human_testing"
dataset = load_dataset(repo_id, split="train")

# Exclude the heavy 'trajectory' column to save memory
light_dataset = dataset.remove_columns(['trajectory'])
df = light_dataset.to_pandas()

⚠️ Note on Memory: The trajectory data is quite large. If you try to convert the entire dataset (including trajectories) directly into a Pandas DataFrame, your Kaggle notebook will likely crash due to an OOM (Out of Memory) error. When using DataFrames, please drop the trajectory column first and parse the trajectory data separately/individually.

2. Extracting and Using Trajectory Data (Streaming)

import json
from datasets import load_dataset

repo_id = "magic-sword/arc_agi_3_public_demo_human_testing"
stream_dataset = load_dataset(repo_id, split="train", streaming=True)

# Process trajectories individually
for idx, record in enumerate(stream_dataset.take(5)):
    trajectory_obj = json.loads(record['trajectory'])

Future Plans

Looking ahead, I want to enhance this dataset by adding explanations of the "human thought process" behind each step in the trajectory. Mimicking not just the actions, but the actual reasoning behind them, could be a powerful weapon for AI long-term planning.

That said, annotating all this reasoning by myself is going to be a massive, time-consuming task…

What do you think? I'd love to hear your thoughts on utilizing this human dataset for ARC-AGI-3, or any feedback on the notebook!
